findings.title: A permanently incomplete explored branch traps the fixed queue without a terminal rejection receipt.

findings.actualControlFlow: A legitimate complete=false branch (for example a deterministic match/round cap) is returned normally by the branch worker and stored in the completed task journal. After all32exploration task receipts arrive, the mean loop throws "exploration branch incomplete: root rejected". It writes no root-report/terminal rejection. On resume the fixed phase sees all32keys, so has zero pending worlds and reaches the same throw. readPilotStatuses sees no terminal report, and the queue allows only this first root forever.
findings.impact: The branch correctly cannot teach a strong label, but a nonfatal rejected pilot root cannot be accounted for and the prelocked source queue cannot advance. Repeated ordinal windows merely consume budget on the same irreparable frontier. This defeats the advertised bounded rejection/progress path; it is not a demand to reroll or remove a failed world.
findings.requiredClosure: Distinguish an interrupted/missing result that may resume the same world from a permanently incomplete cap result. Persist an identity-bound terminal rejection/evidence receipt that advances the fixed prefix while fullyAdjudicated=false and supported=false. Never count it toward12complete or4supported and never replace its source or world.

findings.title: Partial-statistics recovery changes the immutable validated-proof path on a later resume.
findings.actualControlFlow: Leave an unparseable original stats-result.json. Exec2 correctly recomputes the same fixed raw/seed/kernel into stats-recompute-exec-2-T.json, admits it, and appends statistics:validated with that path. If interrupted after this proof but before the root report, exec3 again begins with the still-unparseable original, recomputes identical bytes into a new exec3 timestamped path, and appends the same proof key with a different statsPath. appendBranch rejects it as "completed branch identity changed" even though the statistics hashes agree.
findings.impact: This is a legitimate repeated-interruption state. The newly advertised recovery is not idempotent and cannot finish the root without changing protected journal evidence. The reduced probe uses fully typed, admitted synthetic all-zero raw g+W statistics; it does not depend on a fake positive label or any NN score.
findings.requiredClosure: When a validated proof already exists, first reuse/verify its bound statsPath and root/input/kernel/pair/output digests, and compare any deterministic recomputation to those bytes. Alternatively use a stable canonical recovery artifact and preserve the original partial file. Do not create a new proof address on every resume, delete the proof, alter worlds, or overwrite evidence.
